description: Port Kill helps you find and free ports and caches blocking your dev work.

summary.one_liner: Port Kill is a Rust CLI and status bar tool that finds and frees ports blocking development work, manages dev caches, and orchestrates local services.
summary.what_it_does: It lists processes holding ports and kills them, either by positional port numbers, a one-shot --list, or a --reset of common dev ports. Guard mode watches ports and can auto-restart processes, and Smart Restart re-runs a killed process with its saved command. Service detection finds npm scripts, docker-compose services, Procfile entries and Python apps, and --up/--down/--status manage services defined in a .port-kill.yaml file. A cache subcommand lists, cleans, backs up and restores caches for Rust, JS, Python, Java, npx, and several model/tool caches. It also offers a security audit mode, remote checks over SSH, presets, scripting, and an MCP server for use from editors like Cursor.
use_cases: free a port stuck by a leftover dev server
clean up node_modules, target, and other dev caches
orchestrate multiple local services from one YAML file
watch a port and auto-restart a crashed dev server
check which processes are listening on dev ports over SSH
let an AI assistant in Cursor or Claude kill processes on ports
notable: Two binaries: a macOS status bar app and a cross-platform pure CLI (port-kill-console)
Combined port killer and dev cache cleaner with timestamped backups and restore
Service orchestration with dependency-ordered startup via .port-kill.yaml
Scriptable API such as clearPort(), guardPort() and killFile()
MCP server so AI editors can list, kill and clean ports
caveats: GUI status bar app is macOS only; console binary is the cross-platform option
Windows install requires a full terminal restart for PATH changes to take effect
Vercel and Cloudflare cache cleaning need separate API tokens
keywords: stop whatever is running on my port
